new_entities.name: Bempedoic acid in statin-intolerant patients
aliases: ATP citrate lyase inhibition in statin-intolerant patients
new_entities.description: Use of bempedoic acid as lipid-lowering therapy in adults who are unable or unwilling to take statins because of intolerance.

new_entities.name: Major adverse cardiovascular events
new_entities.description: Composite cardiovascular outcomes such as cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, or coronary revascularization.

edges.effect_quant: CLEAR Outcomes showed a lower primary MACE rate with bempedoic acid in statin-intolerant patients (HR 0.87). Randomized-trial meta-analysis found the same pooled MACE effect size (RR 0.87), and the primary-prevention subgroup of CLEAR Outcomes showed a larger benefit (HR 0.70).
edges.population: adults at high cardiovascular risk who are statin intolerant or unwilling to continue statins because of adverse effects
edges.mechanism: Bempedoic acid inhibits ATP citrate lyase upstream of HMG-CoA reductase, lowering LDL cholesterol without the same degree of skeletal-muscle exposure associated with statin intolerance.
edges.summary: This has become a much stronger edge since CLEAR Outcomes. The benefit is modest in absolute terms, but it is clinically meaningful because it applies to a group that previously had fewer evidence-based lipid-lowering options.
edges.caveats: The magnitude of benefit varies by baseline risk and prevention setting, and adverse effects such as gout and hyperuricemia still matter. The edge is best framed as a useful statin-intolerance fallback, not a wholesale statin replacement.

evidence.citation: Nissen SE et al 2023 N Engl J Med
evidence.notes: Bempedoic Acid and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Statin-Intolerant Patients. CLEAR Outcomes.

effect_quant.comparator: primary MACE endpoint in CLEAR Outcomes with bempedoic acid versus placebo
